newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan zinc smelter plans 20,000-tonne expansion.
newsitem.headline: Japan zinc smelter plans 20,000-tonne expansion.

text.p: Akita Zinc Co has decided to boost capacity at its Iijima zinc smelter by a modest 20,000 tonnes per year, although the extra capacity is not likely to come on line until next year, a source close to the smelter said.

The source said the two billion yen expansion was intended to meet strong domestic demand and to make up for a small part of the domestic capacity lost after the closure of two Japanese smelters in the past two years.

A spokeswoman for Dowa Mining Co, which holds a majority stake in Akita Zinc, confirmed that a decision had been made to proceed with the expansion, although she said no decision had been made on the timing of the project. She declined to comment on its cost.
The expansion will raise Iijima's annual capacity to 176,000 tonnes from 156,000 tonnes.
Nippon Mining and Metals Co and Mitsubishi Materials Corp, the two companies which shut smelters in the past two years, are among the four other shareholders in Akita Zinc.
A Japanese trade paper reported two weeks ago that Akita had decided to lift capacity, although no time frame had been set. Dowa said at that time that no final decision had been made.
Akita has been considering the expansion since the first half of last year.

Although the expansion is tiny relative to global capacity, output plans of zinc mines and smelters for this year are now under close scrutiny, as mining and smelting companies are in the middle of sensitive talks on treatment charges for 1997.
The timing of any cuts or expansion in mining or smelting output is also being carefully monitored.
Higher smelter output relative to mines' concentrate supplies would strengthen the miners' hand in arguing for a reduction in the treatment charges they pay the smelters.
The source also said that Iijima, Japan's biggest and newest zinc smelter, was internationally competitive and would remain so even at an exchange rate of 100 yen to the dollar.

The strength of the dollar, which recently rose to four-year highs above 122 yen, has boosted Japanese smelters' profits as the treatment charges they receive from mining companies are denominated in dollars.
